Reference: Sava et al. 2009 J Biol Chem 284:18194 (PMID 19395379)
Manipulation and readout: Adhesion of E. faecalis 12030 to Caco-2 cells, tested by competitive binding, enzymatic digestion and reduced sulfation
Result: Heparin and heparan sulfate mediated adhesion, chondroitin sulfate B did not. The bacterial ligand is a sugar, not a protein. Pre-treatment with diglucosyldiacylglycerol (DGlcDAG) blocked adhesion.
Implication for this review: The anchor glycolipid is itself the glycosaminoglycan-binding ligand. The authors describe it as acting either in its own right or as a partial structure of lipoteichoic acid.

Manipulation and readout: Deletion of bgsA, an anchor glucosyltransferase
Result: DGlcDAG was lost and MGlcDAG accumulated. The LTA molecule became longer, hydrophobicity fell, biofilm accumulation stopped, Caco-2 adhesion was impaired and the strain was cleared early from the mouse bloodstream. Overexpression increased biofilm.
Implication for this review: Deleting an anchor glycosyltransferase changes backbone length, so the simultaneous change across several layers seen for dlt deletion holds for the anchor as well.

Manipulation and readout: Deletion of bgsB, an anchor glucosyltransferase
Result: Glycolipid was lost entirely. LTA content rose fourfold and the backbone lengthened. Caco-2 adhesion fell by half, biofilm was impaired and the strain was cleared early from the bloodstream.
Implication for this review: The anchor glycosyltransferases set both the amount and the length of LTA.

Manipulation and readout: Double mutant, bgsA deletion combined with lgt deletion
Result: Membrane lipoprotein content rose from 9.4% to 35.8%. TLR2-dependent activity increased and mouse lethality rose by 70%. Introducing the lgt deletion abolished TNF-alpha induction.
Implication for this review: The anchor genotype changes lipoprotein content fourfold, so the genotype problem and the contamination problem meet in the same gene.

Reference: Deininger 2007 / Matsuzaki 2022 (the two existing counter-examples for the anchor)
Manipulation and readout: Removal of gentiobiose from synthetic LTA; comparison of three species sharing a Hex2 anchor
Result: No change in cytokine induction; large differences in IgA activity
Implication for this review: Both counter-examples are TLR2-cytokine or IgA readouts. They measure precisely what the anchor does not determine, and do not measure what it does: adhesion, aggregation and membrane composition.

Manipulation and readout: This review has classified the anchor layer as high in predictability and low in functional determination, on the strength of two counter-examples. Both counter-examples are cytokine or IgA readouts. Change the readout and the anchor determines adhesion, biofilm, membrane hydrophobicity, LTA length, LTA amount, lipoprotein content and persistence in vivo.

All of this evidence is in Enterococcus, not in lactic acid bacteria, and reviews of LTA have not cited it. No characterised anchor glycosyltransferase deletion mutant exists in lactic acid bacteria; bgsA and bgsB mutants have existed in Enterococcus since 2009 and are cited here as the control case.
